experiment_description: Gas-phase methyl iodide (CH3I) at 15 torr and room temperature was studied by time-resolved optical birefringence in a collinear pump-probe geometry. A Ti:sapphire ultrafast source at 800 nm with approximately 110–120 fs pulse duration was split into a strong pump arm carrying about 90% of the energy and a weak probe arm carrying about 10%. The pump beam at 800 nm was sent through a 4-f pulse-shaping system containing two gratings and a Jenoptik dual-mask 640-pixel spatial light modulator at the Fourier plane. The probe was frequency doubled in a BBO crystal to produce a weak 400 nm readout pulse. The probe polarization was set to 45 degrees relative to the pump, and the transmitted probe polarization was analyzed after the gas cell using a quarter-wave plate, Wollaston prism, and balanced photodetection. The pump spectral phase was either transform-limited, with no imposed phase, or cubic, of the form Phi(omega)=b_tilde*(omega-omega0)^3, where omega is optical angular frequency, omega0 is the pulse center angular frequency, and b_tilde is the imposed cubic spectral-phase coefficient. Delay scans of the induced birefringence were recorded around the CH3I half-revival windows at approximately 1.5*T_rev near 100 ps, 2.5*T_rev near 167 ps, and 5.5*T_rev near 367 ps. For the cubic-phase measurements, the applied b_tilde values were 2.0e7 fs^3 at 1.5*T_rev, 3.4e7 fs^3 at 2.5*T_rev, and 6.8e7 fs^3 at 5.5*T_rev. The dependent observable was the temporal morphology of the induced birefringence revival waveform at the selected half-revival delays.

transform_limited_half_revival_morpholog.description: Observed temporal morphology of the CH3I half-revival birefringence signals at the selected long-delay half-revival windows after excitation by a transform-limited 800 nm pump pulse.

cubic_phase_precompensated_half_revival_.description: Observed temporal morphology of the CH3I half-revival birefringence signals at the selected half-revival windows after excitation by the corresponding cubic-phase-shaped 800 nm pump pulses.

experiment_description: Gas-phase carbon dioxide (CO2) was studied by the same collinear time-resolved optical birefringence apparatus: an approximately 110–120 fs, 800 nm ultrafast laser was split into a 90% pump arm and 10% probe arm; the pump was passed through a 4-f pulse shaper with a Jenoptik spatial light modulator; the probe was frequency doubled to 400 nm in BBO; the probe polarization was set to 45 degrees relative to the pump; and induced birefringence was detected using a quarter-wave plate, Wollaston prism, and balanced photodetector. CO2 alignment traces were recorded for an unshaped 120 fs pump near the early 3/4*T_rev revival and near the long-delay 32*T_rev revival. Additional CO2 traces were acquired from 1380 ps to 1412 ps after excitation using an 800 nm pump pulse with a cubic spectral phase designed to pre-compensate centrifugal-distortion dephasing at the 32*T_rev revival. Measurements were performed at 293 K and at 403 K; the higher temperature was used to increase thermal occupation of the v=1 bending vibrational manifold of CO2. The shaped-pulse traces were normalized to the 32+3/4 ground-vibrational-level revival feature. The dependent observables were the time-domain revival waveform morphology and the number of temporally separated rotational-vibrational alignment contributions resolved in the long-delay shaped-pulse trace.

early_unshaped_alignment_feature_duratio.description: Approximate temporal duration of the short-delay CO2 alignment revival feature produced by the unshaped 120 fs pump pulse near the 3/4*T_rev revival.

long_delay_unshaped_revival_morphology.description: Observed morphology of the CO2 birefringence revival near the 32*T_rev delay after excitation by an unshaped 120 fs pump pulse.

cubic_phase_long_delay_resolved_componen.description: Number of temporally separated CO2 rotational-vibrational alignment contributions observed in the 1380–1412 ps long-delay trace after excitation by the cubic-phase-shaped pump pulse.

time_domain_l_doubling_resolved.description: Whether the long-delay cubic-phase-shaped CO2 birefringence measurement directly resolved separated alignment transients associated with l-doubling-related rotational-vibrational contributions.
